title: The app, tab by tab
text: app opens Stoney Lake, Ontario, receivers. Another water body uploaded GeoTIFF water depth land NA. sidebar choose regular grid random draw, number receivers, random seed minimum receiver depth, press Generate. click map adds removes one receiver, CSV file receivers can uploaded. Generate default settings places 20 receivers grid, seed 1, least 1 m deep. Read depth raster app opens . SpatRaster Stoney Lake depth zero negative metres land NA. cells 100 m square, UTM zone 17N (EPSG 32617). Set water shallower minimum receiver depth NA, app . cells left ones receiver may occupy. Place receivers left arraydesign::place_receivers(). returns one row per receiver, position depth deploy_z. start receiver file compare candidate layouts, see article designing array files. screenshot shows layout app. colour receivers coverage, section 3 computes.  Map tab Generate Compute coverage default settings.
code: library(terra) # Stoney Lake, the depth raster bundled with the app lake <- rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",                          package = "arraydesignR")) # Count the water cells, and the water cells that hold 0 sum(!is.na(values(lake))) #> [1] 4818 sum(values(lake) == 0, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 56 # Give the range of the depths (m) range(abs(values(lake)), na.rm = TRUE) #> [1]  0.00000 32.49542 # Keep the cells at least 1 m deep deployable <- ifel(abs(lake) >= 1, lake, NA) # Count the cells a receiver may occupy sum(!is.na(values(deployable))) #> [1] 3249 # Place 20 receivers on a regular grid, seed 1 receivers <- arraydesign::place_receivers(deployable, n = 20,                                           method = "grid", seed = 1) # How many receivers, and how deep they sit (m) nrow(receivers) #> [1] 20 range(receivers$deploy_z) #> [1]  1.003954 24.834967

title: The app, tab by tab
text: Detection probability falls distance logistic curve 0.5 d50 0.05 d05. Range model tab set d50 d05 shallow deep receiver depth, interpolated linearly receiver’s depth held constant outside two depths. app defaults, next chunk sets, come range test; replace d50 d05 . R, model fitted range test, varying depth date, goes detfield::de_model() (see article range models detfield). Build default curve detfield::de_logistic(). returns detection model. Read curve 0 m, d50 d05 receiver 1 m deep. curve$predict returns logit, plogis() turns probability. d05 twice d50, detection 0 m 0.95. closer d05 d50, nearer curve starts 1. app leaves cells farther every receiver distance curve falls 0.001, read deeper receiver depth, 35 m.  Range model tab defaults. Open circles mark d50 d05 curves two set depths.
code: # The app defaults: d50 and d05 at a 1 m and a 35 m receiver curve <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),                                depth = c(1, 35)) curve #> <de_model> de_logistic, d50 250/750 m, d05 500/1500 m, depths 1/35 m #>   reads: distance_m, depth_m  #>   sigma: station_hour not given #>   blocked line of sight: curve read at the distance through water # Detection probability at 0, 250 and 500 m from a 1 m receiver plogis(curve$predict(c(0, 250, 500), depth_m = 1)) #> [1] 0.95 0.50 0.05 # The first whole metre at which a 35 m receiver detects with p < 0.001 distance_m <- 0:5000 p_deep <- plogis(curve$predict(distance_m, depth_m = 35)) cutoff_m <- min(distance_m[p_deep < 0.001]) cutoff_m #> [1] 2510

title: The app, tab by tab
text: Compute coverage, sidebar Map tab, gives every water cell probability least one receiver detects one transmission. drawn Map tab, screenshot section 1. coverage Pedersen et al. (2014, Methods Ecology Evolution 5: 1043-1051, https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12255). map four layers: depth, distance water nearest receiver, array detection probability, detection within hour (section 4). Measure distance water receiver water cell, cutoff. detfield::water_distances() returns one row per receiver-cell pair within . Read curve distance detfield::de_field(). returns detection probability receiver cell, warns land lies straight line receiver cell. app keeps default, blocked = 0, behind islands points land map overstates detection. R, negative blocked value detfield::de_model() lowers detection pairs. Combine receivers detfield::system_de(). needs days receiver listened; one day 20 gives coverage layout. Count water cells probability 0.5 , share Map tab’s banner reports.
code: # Distances through water from the 20 receivers, up to the cutoff distances <- detfield::water_distances(   lake, receivers[c("station_id", "x", "y", "deploy_z")],   max_distance = cutoff_m ) nrow(distances) #> [1] 21093 # Detection probability of each receiver at each cell field <- detfield::de_field(distances, curve) #> 52 of 2,304 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the #>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on #>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model. # One listening day for every receiver in the field listening <- data.frame(station_id = field$receivers,                         date = as.Date("2000-01-01")) # Probability that at least one receiver detects one transmission, per cell coverage <- detfield::system_de(field, listening)$p length(coverage) #> [1] 4818 # Cells and share of the water at p >= 0.5 sum(coverage >= 0.5) #> [1] 648 mean(coverage >= 0.5) #> [1] 0.1344956

title: The app, tab by tab
text: Performance tab reads last coverage result, press Compute coverage change layout range model. share 0.5 first tile; next two chunks give two. Count water cells 0.05 . hourly probability p_hour = 1 - (1 - p)^n, n = 3600 / delay transmissions hour mean transmission delay set tab (120 s start, n = 30). assumes successive transmissions detected independently; detection clustered time, p_hour overstates chance detection. arraydesign::coverage_summary() counts cells single receiver reaches threshold . returns one row per threshold. “one receiver” columns tab’s table, 0.05 0.5.  Performance tab Compute coverage default settings.
code: # Cells and share of the water at p >= 0.05 sum(coverage >= 0.05) #> [1] 2216 mean(coverage >= 0.05) #> [1] 0.4599419 # Probability of at least one detection in an hour, 30 transmissions p_hour <- 1 - (1 - coverage)^(3600 / 120) # Cells and share of the water at p_hour >= 0.95 sum(p_hour >= 0.95) #> [1] 1837 mean(p_hour >= 0.95) #> [1] 0.3812785 # Cells reached by the best single receiver at 0.05 and 0.5 single_receiver <- arraydesign::coverage_summary(field,                                                  thresholds = c(0.05, 0.5)) single_receiver #>   threshold n_cells n_water_cells     share n_receivers #> 1      0.05    2171          4818 0.4506019          20 #> 2      0.50     636          4818 0.1320050          20

title: The app, tab by tab
text: Simulation tab walks animals water correlated random walk, sends transmissions random delay shortest longest delay, receiver hears transmission, , range model. detection rate animal share transmissions heard least one receiver. Set movement model arraydesign::crw_model(). values app’s starting ones; species measured . set walk species, see article movement models. Walk 20 animals 6 hours lake arraydesign::simulate_tracks(). returns one row per animal per time step. Send transmissions along track delay drawn 120 180 s. arraydesign::simulate_transmissions() returns one row per transmission. Build detection field whole lake. field section 3 cutoff, animal can anywhere lake. Detect transmission curve arraydesign::simulate_detections(). returns number receivers heard transmission. article part simulation shows every table tracks detections. Summarise detection rate across animals. Count animal-hours least one detection. chunks print numbers tiles Simulation tab . rates depend movement model range model, use compare layouts settings.  Simulation tab one run default settings, 20 animals 6 hours, seed 1.
code: # Correlated random walk: mean step 30 m (SD 15 m) per 60 s, turning SD 40 walk <- arraydesign::crw_model(step_mean = 30, step_sd = 15, turn_sd = 40,                                time_step_s = 60) walk #> <movement_model> 1 state  #> time step: 60 s #> source: crw_model(): gamma steps, mean 30 m and sd 15 m per 60 s; wrapped #>   normal turns, sd 40 degrees # 20 animals, 360 steps of 60 s each, seed 1 tracks <- arraydesign::simulate_tracks(lake, walk, n_animals = 20,                                        n_steps = 6 * 3600 / 60, seed = 1) nrow(tracks) #> [1] 7220 # Transmissions at a random delay of 120 to 180 s, seed 1 transmissions <- arraydesign::simulate_transmissions(   tracks, tag_delay = c(120, 180), seed = 1 ) nrow(transmissions) #> [1] 2884 # Distances through water from the 20 receivers to every water cell distances_lake <- detfield::water_distances(   lake, receivers[c("station_id", "x", "y", "deploy_z")] ) # Detection probability of each receiver at every water cell field_lake <- detfield::de_field(distances_lake, curve) #> 52 of 2,304 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the #>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on #>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model. # Detect each transmission, with no extra variation between receivers detections <- arraydesign::simulate_detections(   transmissions, field_lake, overdispersion = "none", seed = 1 ) # Transmissions heard by at least one receiver heard <- detections$transmissions$n_detections > 0 sum(heard) #> [1] 461 # Share of each animal's transmissions heard detection_rate <- tapply(heard, transmissions$path_id, mean) # Mean, SE, median and range of the rate across animals (%) round(100 * c(mean = mean(detection_rate),               se = sd(detection_rate) / sqrt(length(detection_rate)),               median = median(detection_rate),               min = min(detection_rate), max = max(detection_rate)), 1) #>   mean     se median    min    max  #>   16.0    2.9   17.9    0.0   38.2 # Animals never detected sum(detection_rate == 0) #> [1] 4 # Hour of the walk, 0 to 5, of each transmission; the last second counts # in hour 5, as in the app walk_start <- as.POSIXct("2025-01-01", tz = "UTC") hours_in <- as.numeric(difftime(transmissions$datetime, walk_start,                                 units = "hours")) hour_of_walk <- pmin(5, floor(hours_in)) # Whether each animal was heard in each hour heard_by_hour <- tapply(heard, list(transmissions$path_id, hour_of_walk),                         any) sum(heard_by_hour, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 77
